messages.subject: replicating a horizontal timeline of bank consolidation: hints
parts:
Attached is a sort of horizontal timeline showing bank consolidation over time.

I like it and wanted to replicate it, with a view to extending the data to other countries, other time periods, etc..

But I'm not even sure where to start. I'd appreciate hints on the following:

1. what do I call this chart?

2. do you know of anything similar already available with ggplot?

3. can a clever use of horizontal geom_bar() with labels get anywhere close? or would you recommend another approach altogether?

Thanks!

The image may be seen here, where the copyright belongs, I think:

http://www.motherjones.com/politics/2010/01/bank-merger-history

Hi Patrick,

There's an example of one of those Sankey diagrams in one of Hadley Wickham's papers: http://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1198/jcgs.2009.07098

Good luck,

Tom

messages.author: bb977a465f0b4c86
messages.subject: Re: replicating a horizontal timeline of bank consolidation: hints
parts:
As Raphael mentioned, have a look at the riverplot package.

Just a simple example (modified from the example in the package:


nodes <- data.frame( ID= LETTERS[1:5],
                     x= c( 1, 1, 3,1,2 ),
                     y = c(1,2,1,3,2),
                     labels= c( "Node A", "Node B", "Node C", " Node D","Node E" )
)
edges <- list( A= list( C= 10 ), B= list( E= 10 ), D = list(E = 5), E = list(C  =15) )
r <- makeRiver( nodes, edges )
plot( r )
